statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. NVIDIA-led overnight strength remains material, but current broad-index confirmation is moderate and persistent no-retracement NQ structure is not independently verified.
recommendation: Tail remains in the WATCH band while residual NVIDIA repricing persists; the blocking threshold is not met without stronger evidence of sustained mean-reversion failure.
headline: NVIDIA impulse remains positive, while broader confirmation stays moderate
body: Reuters reported NVIDIA up 4.7% after hours and S&P 500 e-mini futures up 0.4%, while the U.S. 10-year yield eased to 4.647% and Brent crude continued lower. The combination supports residual upside risk but does not establish a persistent one-way NQ path.

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 clock-hours, Tail was low through most of Wednesday, moved into WATCH after NVIDIA's delayed earnings-call reversal, reached 24% as the impulse broadened overnight, and eased to 22% as broad futures confirmation moderated.
outlookSummary: Residual NVIDIA repricing keeps current Tail in WATCH, but easing yields and lower oil argue against a block without stronger one-way NQ evidence. The next concentrated risk window is the 12:30 UTC U.S. data cluster and subsequent cash open.

forecast.analysis: Observed NVIDIA-led strength remains visible in broad overnight risk sentiment, but the latest verified evidence shows only moderate index-futures confirmation and does not establish persistent no-retracement NQ structure.

forecast.analysis: If the earnings impulse continues to age without repeated extension, two-way trade would reduce Tail below WATCH despite still-elevated residual event stress.

European pre-open liquidity is a normalization checkpoint; sustained extension would keep the overnight impulse relevant, while ordinary retracements would argue for mixed rather than pathological structure.
At the European cash open, breadth and retracement quality are the key conditional tests; Tail stays low unless renewed directional efficiency develops across index futures and technology.
Early European trade should reveal whether the NVIDIA impulse broadens. Without repeated extension or failed pullbacks, the more likely regime is normalizing two-way price discovery.
Later European trade provides another test of breadth persistence. A renewed one-way technology bid could lift Tail, while cross-asset calm and retracements would keep it low.
As U.S. premarket participation builds, the overnight technology impulse may be re-tested. Tail remains conditional on sustained index-level continuation rather than the earnings headline alone.
Approaching the U.S. data window, event proximity raises Stress. Tail reaches WATCH only conditionally because the scheduled releases are catalysts, not evidence of mean-reversion failure.

The 12:30 UTC U.S. claims and advance trade/inventory releases create a concentrated repricing window. Tail remains WATCH unless the post-release path develops repeated extension with weak retracements.
Post-data price discovery is the key checkpoint. Fast moves that retrace would favor whipsaw stress; sustained extension with failed pullbacks would justify a higher Tail assessment.
The U.S. cash open overlaps the post-data digestion window. Opening-auction continuation would matter only if it persists with shallow pullbacks and broader confirmation.
By the second U.S. cash hour, the initial macro/open impulse should be clearer. Two-way trade would lower Tail; repeated directional extension would preserve WATCH conditions.
Mid-session risk should ease if the data/opening impulse has normalized. Tail remains conditional on whether index futures continue to hold near extremes without meaningful retracement.
Early U.S. afternoon trading typically shifts emphasis from event shock to structure. Normal pullbacks and fading directional efficiency would return the regime toward mixed conditions.
With the main scheduled catalyst absorbed, Tail should remain low unless a new headline or renewed cross-asset alignment creates a fresh one-way index move.
Late-afternoon U.S. trade is a continuation checkpoint. Persistent movement toward session extremes with failed pullbacks would be the principal reason to lift Tail from low levels.
Into the final U.S. cash hour, power-hour continuation is conditional rather than assumed; ordinary retracement and balanced breadth would keep Tail low.
After the cash close, the absence of a new scheduled index-level catalyst favors normalization, while unexpected geopolitical or technology headlines remain residual risks.
Early evening futures trade should be quieter if the prior U.S. session closes without directional stress. Tail remains low absent renewed extension or a fresh catalyst.
Overnight liquidity becomes thinner; isolated moves may increase noise, but Tail requires sustained directional efficiency rather than volatility alone.
Asian pre-open conditions are expected to inherit the prior U.S. close. A calm handoff would keep Tail low, while a fresh technology or geopolitical impulse could reintroduce WATCH risk.
At the start of Asian trading, breadth across technology markets becomes a conditional confirmation test; isolated gains would not by themselves establish pathological NQ structure.
Early Asian session continuation would matter only if it aligns with persistent index-futures extension and weak retracement. Otherwise the regime remains normal.
Later Asian trading remains a handoff period ahead of Friday's larger U.S. policy catalyst. Tail stays low unless new one-way structure is independently verified.
